[The lab]{.eyebrow}

::: {.lead}
We pursue microbiological questions related to ecosystem change and the
surveillance of infectious diseases, addressed through the lens of emerging
next-generation sequencing tools. These topics rely on a One Health approach
that connects human, animal, and environmental health.
:::

Our research has three primary emphases. We track the spread of emerging human
and veterinary pathogens, from SARS-CoV-2 in Alaska to African swine fever virus
in Ukraine. We explore how disturbance shapes the resistome, the environmental
reservoir of antibiotic resistance genes. And we examine how thawing permafrost
affects the microbes in the overlying soil, along with the downstream
consequences for boreal forest plant growth.

The work combines fieldwork, molecular analysis, and experimental laboratory
research with mathematical modeling. Our research team has a commitment to
broadening participation in biomedical research.
